North West Madagascar

Mahajanga

Vibrant Coastal City & Gateway to Madagascar's North-West

The Destination

Mahajanga

Nestled along Madagascar's north-west coast, Mahajanga is a vibrant seaside city known for its golden beaches, rich cultural heritage and spectacular natural attractions. Often overlooked by international travellers, Mahajanga offers an authentic blend of relaxation, adventure and discovery, making it one of Madagascar's most rewarding destinations.

With its warm climate, palm-lined waterfront, colourful markets and proximity to some of the island's most remarkable landscapes, Mahajanga is perfect for travellers seeking a relaxed and immersive experience.

Natural Beauty & Coastal Charm

A City of Colour & Character

Mahajanga enjoys a picturesque setting where the Betsiboka River meets the Mozambique Channel. The region is known for wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets and a laid-back atmosphere. One of the city's most iconic landmarks is the giant Baobab Tree — rumoured to be the oldest baobab in Madagascar — which stands along the waterfront. The combination of Malagasy, African, Arab, Indian and French influences gives Mahajanga a unique and vibrant character found nowhere else in Madagascar.

Experiences

Things to Do in Mahajanga

Ankarafantsika National Park

One of Madagascar's most important protected areas — dry deciduous forests, lemurs, rare birds, chameleons and the beautiful Lake Ravelobe.

Cirque Rouge

Colourful red sandstone cliffs and canyons sculpted by erosion into an extraordinary landscape — one of Madagascar's most striking natural landmarks.

Mahajanga's Beaches

Long stretches of golden sand, warm waters and spectacular sunsets along the coastline overlooking the Mozambique Channel.

The Giant Baobab Tree

Mahajanga's iconic waterfront baobab — rumoured to be the oldest in Madagascar — a beloved local landmark and the city's most photographed attraction.

Wildlife Watching

Excellent opportunities to spot lemurs, endemic birds, reptiles and other unique wildlife throughout the surrounding region's protected areas.

Waterfront & Local Markets

Stroll the lively seafront promenade at sunset, then explore vibrant markets for crafts, spices, fresh produce and traditional Malagasy products.

Accommodation

Where to Stay

Mahajanga offers a diverse range of accommodation from beachfront resorts and boutique hotels to eco-lodges and family-run guesthouses — an excellent base for exploring Madagascar's north-western region.

✦Beachfront accommodation with ocean views
✦Boutique hotels and charming guesthouses
✦Easy access to national parks and natural attractions
✦Fresh seafood and locally inspired cuisine
✦Guided wildlife and cultural excursions
✦A relaxed coastal atmosphere with year-round sunshine

Highlights

  • Ankarafantsika National Park & Lake Ravelobe
  • Cirque Rouge — red sandstone canyons
  • The giant waterfront Baobab Tree
  • Golden beaches & Mozambique Channel sunsets
  • Vibrant local markets & seafront promenade
  • Wildlife — lemurs, endemic birds, chameleons

When to Visit

May – November
Dry season. Best conditions for visiting Ankarafantsika and exploring the region.
June – September
Peak dry season with excellent wildlife sightings.
December – April
Wet season — lush green landscapes but some roads can be difficult.
